speaker: Doctor
text:
The physical examination and dermoscopic evaluation show normal readings, which is concerning given your initial concern for a dermatological condition. Can you tell me exactly where on your body these lesions are located and if you have a history of similar skin issues? Have you had any recent sun exposure or trauma to the area?

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of the largest suspicious lesion.
REQUEST IMAGES: High-resolution magnified view of the lesion surface.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy Findings: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The biopsy results indicating nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within follicular epithelium are highly suspicious for malignancy. To distinguish between a follicular variant of B-cell lymphoma and a cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, do you have any history of systemic symptoms like fevers, night sweats, or significant weight loss? Also, has this lesion been present for more than a year?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Follicular Center Lymphoma or Squamous Cell Carcinoma (pending further histopathological grading).
